# setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)

```

# Problem 1

ny_noaa with `r ncol(ny_noaa)`variables and `r nrow(ny_noaa)` obervations includes daily observation data in different weather stations in New York over 1981–2010 ,such as weather station id，Precipitation (tenths of mm)，date，snowfall,snow depth,maximum temperature and minimum temperature.

The data size is very large and many missing data exist, especially among tmax and tmin.

```{r}
data("ny_noaa")
ny <- ny_noaa

ny_clean = ny |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    prcp_mm = as.numeric(prcp)/ 10,         
    tmax_c = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,          
    tmin_c = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,           
    snow_mm = snow,              
    snwd_mm = snwd
  ) |>
  select(id, date, year, month, day, prcp_mm, snow_mm, snwd_mm, tmax_c, tmin_c)


snow_common = ny_clean |>
  count(snow_mm, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```
The most common snowfall values are 0 (no snow) and 25mm, 13mm, 51mm, etc. Zero is by far the most frequent because most days have no snowfall.

```{r}
jan_july <- ny_clean |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 7, !is.na(tmax_c)) |>
  group_by(id, month, year) |>
  summarise(avg_tmax = mean(tmax_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(month_lab = factor(month, levels = c(1, 7), labels = c("January", "July")))

ggplot(jan_july, aes(x = year, y = avg_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), se = FALSE, color = "darkred", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ month_lab) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature by Station",
    subtitle = "January vs July, 1981–2010",
    x = "Year", y = "Average Tmax (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

January temperatures show more year-to-year fluctuation and a slight upward trend at some stations. July temperatures are higher and more stable. A few stations appear as outliers, one station with unusually low value around 1987 July and one statioj with very lower tmax around 1982 Jan in particular.

```{r}

ggplot(ny_clean |> 
         filter(!is.na(tmax_c), 
                !is.na(tmin_c)), 
       aes(x = tmin_c, y = tmax_c)) +
  geom_hex(bins = 80) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, 
              linetype = "dashed", 
              color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Tmax vs Tmin (all observations)",
       x = "Tmin (°C)", 
       y = "Tmax (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()

ny_clean |>
  filter(snow_mm > 0, 
         snow_mm < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow_mm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2, 
               fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of positive snowfall (<100 mm) by year",
       x = "Year", y = "Snowfall (mm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7))
```
tmax and tmin are strongly positively associated. The snowfall distribution shows that most non-zero snowfalls are modest; extreme values are rare and the pattern is fairly consistent across years, with some years having heavier tails, for example, snowfall data in 2006 has heavy upper tail.

# Problem 2

```{r}

covar = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
  skip = 4,
  na = c(".", "", "NA"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  janitor::clean_names()

accel = read_csv(
  "data/nhanes_accel.csv",
  na = c(".", "", "NA"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  janitor::clean_names()


covar_clean = covar |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    education = factor(education,
                       levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                       labels = c("Less than HS", "HS equivalent", "More than HS"),
                       ordered = TRUE)
  ) |>
  filter(age >= 21, !is.na(sex), !is.na(education), !is.na(age))

accel_long = accel |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minute",
    values_to = "mims",
    names_prefix = "min"
  ) |>
  mutate(minute = as.integer(minute))

nhanes = accel_long |>
  inner_join(covar_clean, by = "seqn")
```
```{r}

tab = nhanes |>
  distinct(seqn, sex, education) |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

knitr::kable(tab, caption = "Number of men and women by education category")
```

There are more participants with “More than high school” education. Sex balance is reasonably even within each education category, but for high school equivalent education level, men are more than women.

```{r}

nhanes |>
  distinct(seqn, age, sex, education) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(title = "Age distributions by education and sex",
       x = "Age", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```
In "Less than HS" and "HS equivalent" groups, there are more young women than young men and more elder men than elder women , but among "More than HS" people, young men are much more than young women. Also, there are more elder 
participants than younger ones in "Less than HS" and "HS equivalent", but for "More than HS" group, young people are more than elder people.
